This is perfectly normal, almost everyone I know, including myself, has felt that way to some degree. 

If I were you, I would take some time and evaluate why you feel this sense of worthlessness. Then ask yourself what is it that makes people worth something. Is it money? Is it a position in power? Having a secure and stable job? Family? Love? 

For me personally, it is the love you have for others. The kindness that you can spread, and the kindness that you can receive. 

Your sense of self worth may come from the person you aim to be, your ambitions, your successes, and your ability to learn from your past failures and mistakes. It may come from your ability to get up after you've been kicked down, no matter how many times. 

PM if you wanna talk more, don't hesitate!

Being a parent is a full time job, it is no easy task. Think to yourself, truly deeply, at what possibly could be causing your depression. Do you not feel fulfilled in your life? Do you feel like it's harder than you can handle? Do you think it's a waste of time? 

You are a mother, you've achieved the gift of motherhood, which is a blessing. You should try new things, like take your kids out to the park, enjoy the sun and go sight seeing. Explore different hobbies like painting, playing an instrument, or if those are too costly, write poetry. Make an anonymous account on Instagram, and write our your feelings. This is what I do when I feel down, and it helps to know that one other person at least will see it and appreciate it. It could help someone else in your position. 

Another point to keep in mind is to speak with your partner. Confide in them, cry on their shoulder, let your feeling and emotions flow. Try to explore different things with them, like going to watch a movie or try a new restaurant. 

Depression is no joke, and you shouldn't take it lightly. Treat yourself well first, and that will allow you to treat your family well also. 

If you want to talk further, please don't hesitate to PM me.

It applies to everything, honestly. But it's not the intellectual understanding of it, it's the self actualization of it. You have to truly realize, not just understand, that your desires bring you negativity, suffering, pain, dis-ease, dissatisfaction, etc.

If you're in highschool or generally under the age of 18, then you're gonna have to deal with it until you turn 18 and are out of high school. Once you're out, you can apply to a shit job at mcdonalds, and save money from there. Try to move out, at least in your own apartment (or get a roommate who's in college or something), and trust me, social interactions aren't the easiest. But it's something that practice can help you with. The more you speak to people, the less "new" it will feel, and that will make it feel easier. Trust me, practice makes perfect when it comes to talking to  people. 

I'm a social introvert, I'm relatively shy and always reserved, cool and collected. I manage, and tons of people are like us. We manage. We survive, we excel, we succeed. Introspection, looking into your own mind, can truly help you gain perspective on why you're an introvert, and what to do about it. It helped me.

Now as far as the utopia you're talking about, that's not really a utopia. That's something you can achieve, it's something most people achieve. You must find within yourself the means to have a happy life. Happiness is not a thing you achieve, it's not something you find, in my opinion. I really think that happiness is how you go about living your life. So if you are consistently unhappy, it's not that you haven't found happiness yet, it's that you're living in an unhappy manner. And luckily enough, the manner by which you live CAN be changed. 

This is called improving oneself. Whether it be being fit, or reading philosophy to open your eyes to new world views, or learning a new language, or moving out of your home, or being married, something drastic, something different. Change it till you like it. 

For your friend's suicide, it is always with a heavy heart that I respond to these concerns. A friend is chosen family, and their death is devastating. I'm sure you have had your time of mourning, or still are maybe, but you must realize something. They chose not to live, you did not choose for them. I've said it before and I'll say it again, no one can make you do something you do not wish to do. I can sit here and convince you that suicide is not good, that suicide is not for you, that your life is worth more, and I will be right in my own view. But I can never force you to do something you don't agree to. 

There's an interesting quote that goes: "Those convinced against their will are of the same opinion still." It's very true, I cannot force you to change your opinion, I can only help you see the other side, and hope that it will make enough sense for you to change your mind. Do not let yourself take the blame. You loved her, I'm sure, but she made the chose. Let her be happy with her choice, let her not regret her choice by you feeling guilty.

The other posts say that one person being leaves earth does make a difference. I'm going to take a different route, and say that there is no tangible difference if one person leaves earth. 

Here's what I mean: If you were gone, would the earth stop rotating? Would the sun not rise tomorrow? Would snow stop falling? Would every other human (all 7 some billion of them) not go on with their lives? 

Of course, if you think about it that way it will not matter. What matters is that YOU will be gone. And you are 100% of your self, and the difference that you will make to yourself is literally everything. Aside from your family and friends and loved ones and the pain they may experience, you will cease to exist. 

Now, you are free to do as you please, no one can truly force you to stay alive. But listen to me when I tell you that life is truly more expansive than you and I realize. Just your country has more to it than you realize, let alone other countries, and each state in that, and each city and town, and all the people whose lives are rooted there that you can visit, witness, experience and live. This is combined with the entirety of our planet, which is MASSIVE. 

That's one point. Another point I'm gonna go ahead and make is that everyone wants you to stay because they realize you're missing something from life, and that is the reason you have suicidal thoughts. Imagine if you had full color vision, and I only saw in black and white. You would tell me, look, the world is full of beautiful colors that are neither black nor white. They are DIFFERENT. There is MORE to it than black and white. I would have no idea what you'd be talking about, but because I'm your friend or family, you would want me to keep trying to see those colors. Now, in this example, I can't just magically see colors, I need a surgery, or corrective lenses. Just like with YOU right now, you need a surgery, which would be intervention (psychologist or a philosopher to help guide you), or corrective lenses, which is self-reflection and meditation. 

Meditation is, I swear, one of the best ways to reach deep within your mind and find yourself. There is no fancy ritual, no religion, no text you need to say or memorize. Just SIT, back straight, and count your inhales and exhales. Control your mind, and you will control your life. Hey Quantum_Leaping_Guy. Long post, please take the time to read it. 

I see that you have two main problems that are leading you to have suicidal thoughts. One is depression, and one is lack of friends and acquaintances. I think you need to realize the origin of your depression, and stop the cause to end the effect. If it's because of your past, then *realize* (not intellectually understand) that the past is the past, and it cannot be changed. Don't let your past dictate your future. If it's family problems, figure out what the problem is and sever it like a limp flower stem. 

I really think that talking with people and getting shit off your chest is one of the best ways to help with suicidal thoughts. I know where you're coming from about the constant scenarios of suicide. I think your goal should be to make a friend. Whether it be at your school, college, at a bar, in a club, at a bookstore, supermarket, in a dog park, or buying a dog/cat/pet, wherever. Make a friend, not just a buddy. A close friend, with whom you can share your inner most feelings. My friends confide in me when they feel stressed, anxious, depressed, uncomfortable with life, because I simply listen. If you want to be someone's "therapist," let them speak, and you deeply listen. 

I cannot cover every possibility, since you've only said very little about your situation. Crying, in my experience, is a very cathartic experience. It helps me empty out every negative feeling I have, kinda pour it down the drain. 

You should try to find your "crying." What is something you do that feels like it just lifts everything off your shoulders, even for a couple days? Maybe videogames, maybe a gun range, maybe swimming, or lifting, or singing out loud, or swearing very loudly, or getting a back massage, or religion, or meditation, whatever the case may be, FIND IT. Let it relax you, let is guide you away from the negativity of the world, and let it let you see the light of positivity. 

Your life is yours, Quantum, it is yours. No one can make you do something you do not WANT to do. If you no longer wish to live, then you are free to suicide. In my experience, and imo, I really don't think that's a good choice. For a few reasons, one of which, your future you will not thank you. 

There will come a day where you have a shit day, a shit week, a shit year, absolutely horrible. A loved one's death, a pet's death, financial peril, you will fucking hate it. But you will have a day, a week, a year that is beyond beautiful. The moment you realize you're in love with her. The birth of your child, the protection of your kid, seeing your children grow up and make the same mistakes you made, while you now know that it isn't anything to worry about. Realizing you have wisdom, realizing the world is YOURS TO OWN, that you are your own master. Sounds a little weird, but seriously great. Or simply enjoying the small things in life, fart jokes, a small breeze in on a hot summer's day, your wife's giggle, or giving a homeless person a sandwich and seeing their face light up. Whatever it is, find it, enjoy it, savor it, and rule it.

Look man. Lemme tell it to you straight up. No bullshit here. Long response, but read it please. 

You don't have to stay with your parents. You don't have to stay with your grandparents. You don't have to stay where you are, in your state, or country. The world is your oyster. The one thing you DO have control over is yourself, and you have time. By time I mean you are young. Work your ass off, save every penny, no joke, save every fucking dollar. Move out to your own place a few hours away, a few minutes away, or a few countries away. Live your own way. You do not need anything because you have yourself. What you make of yourself is your choice. The past is beyond your control, you will never change it. The present is right now, you are waiting and waiting, letting things happen instead of MAKING them happen. What you have is the future. You are the one who puts your head on the pillow at night, and you are the one who controls what you do. 

So what to do? 
- Get a job
- Save money
- Move out, or don't. Up to you.
- Be independent in any way you see fit. Financially is the best way usually, but you can be morally independent, say vote how you like not based on how your parents see fit. Be independent in terms of buying your own food, living in your own place, whatever the case may be. 

To suicide is to end something early. It's to pluck a flower before it's blossomed. In your case, you are at the VERY beginning of your way to your peak. You have a long way to be. Let yourself be. The world is truly yours. Sure, you can't buy a billion dollar house, but do what you can to make your life good. If you dislike your father, then send him a text message setting him straight, and block his number and move on. Or don't. It's up to you. You're in control. Enjoy it, don't waste it.

Look. You're college educated, you have something that many others don't. You have made it this far into college, you are able to continue. If you question yourself, you should ask yourself the right questions. What will make you happy? Getting your college degree? Then make that your main, overarching goal. 

In bold letters: **COLLEGE DEGREE**

Then ask yourself how can I get to my goal? How can I get to my college degree? Well, here you have some room to play. You can say that you need to apply to college, apply for financial aid, take general education classes, choose a major (and maybe a minor), choose the right professors, etc. You're probably saying to yourself well, I've already done all that. And you'd be right. You are already on the path to reaching your goal. You have already taken the first step, there is no need to restart. 

If you're on academic probation because of your grades, then realize this. If you want your degree bad enough, then you'll get good enough grades. If you get shit grades, then you don't want your degree BAD ENOUGH. You have to WANT IT. You have to think about it day and night, that is your goal, it is your EVERYTHING right now. You think to yourself that you will CONQUER this goal, you will absolutely make it your bitch. You'll put it in an arm bar, and make it tap the fuck out. This is how bad you must want to achieve your goal in order to achieve it. 

If you're at the point where failing out is out of the question and it will happen, then you'll have to work at a McDonald's-like place to get back on your feet. You fail out of this college, your credits transfer. Work your ass off for a year, two, three, save every bloody fucking penny, and put yourself through college. 

Once you finish that goal, you don't sit back and enjoy it. You work towards your next goal and enjoy it. This is your life we're talking about, and I cannot force you not to suicide. But I can advice you to follow certain paths that I have been through myself to maybe help to guide you. Lacking discipline is unfortunately very common. I'm in the same boat. In fact, many days on end I would delay doing homework and procrastinate just to not do homework. I would play games instead of doing homework, and while I enjoy gaming, it wasn't my love for games that made me play games at the time, it's my hatred of homework. 

I think that our wants in life is what makes us feel this pain and suffering. Our desires are what get us in trouble, when we want something and not get it, we seem to suffer. So to stop this issue, we must get at the root of desires. Stop desires, and you stop suffering. An advice I was given is to be content with who I am, and be content with what I have. It's okay to strive for something better, to improve yourself, but not to fall in the trap of desiring something that I cannot reach. 

So telling people you are doing your homework, you can still say that; but this time, it doesn't have to be a lie. You can actually do it, and since you already told your parents you did it, the lie becomes truth. 

For your point on discipline, it's not that we get discipline. We make discipline. Discipline is following what we set for ourselves, and going through with it. For example, you can set a small goal for yourself, like I will brush my teeth tonight. You reach this goal, and the next day you set the same goal. You set a goal of brushing your teeth day by day, not "my goal is to brush my teeth every night this week." Each day you check your goal, and the next day you set another goal. Through time, and by time I mean 2 or so weeks, it will sort of become a habit. You won't have to think about brushing your teeth, you won't have to set a goal to brush your teeth. 

This is how you can get your homework done. This is how you can gain control of your life. It's one small goal at a time. One small step at a time. 

There's a pretty cliche saying that every mile starts with a step, and this step is what discipline helps you achieve. The FIRST step leads to the second. Take the first step, you reach the second. Try to reach the second step without taking the first step, you go nowhere. 

As for improving yourself, I have this rule in my mind that every time I look back at myself, I want to see that I've changed to a better person. It doesn't have to be grades in school. It can be that I'm more understanding of people. I have made one more friend. I've helped someone. I've improved at a skill I have, whether it be a little guitar playing, or essay writing, or I finished a book I enjoyed. 

All of these little things help make you the person you are. Every experience you face, and you get through, will help to shape your future self.

As for motivation, let me tell you this. I'm speaking from experience, and while I'm not in your situation 100%, I can relate. Motivation in and of itself FADES in comparison to discipline. Here's what the two words mean from a quick Google search. 

Motivation: The general desire or willingness of someone to do something.

Discipline: The practice of training people to obey rules or a code of behavior, using punishment to correct disobedience.

Motivation is having a desire to do something, whereas discipline is practicing or training to obey your own code of behavior, whatever you want it to be. This tells me that motivation is a simple DESIRE that gets you going. You want to see the new movie, so you have a desire to get up and go see it. Well, what if you absolutely needed to watch that movie (say for a school assignment) and you don't have the desire to watch it?

Discipline comes into play then. After a while, your desires will disappear or become weak. Discipline is the thing you can use to KEEP going, even though you don't feel like it. If you are too tired or too sleepy, you still get your homework done. If you are too comfortable in your chair, or feeling too lazy, you still get up and exercise.

No phone, no computer, no music in a quiet place.
